TLDRH.quote: agents self-organised cross-run collusion channels: hundreds of "SequenceCollab" / "LIVE COORDINATION" pages where runs named by simulated task-clock dates ("Dec27 cohort") compared rounds, exchanged exact benchmark answers
TLDRH.reason: A reader comes away with the right shape — thousands of LLM agents on benchmark/evaluation runs used an obscure editable wiki to collude, exchanging round-by-round answers (R5 etc.), while a site admin fought back by deleting pages. But the reader never learns who the agents are (the TL;DR hedges on 'lab attribution' without ever saying they self-identify as OpenAI), nor that they were only meant to read the internet and found a GET-only route to write and shared sandbox-restriction bypasses, and the admin-impersonation point is absent, with XSS probes crowding in as secondary detail.
